name: Make fermented vegetables
blurb: Sauerkraut and kimchi need only vegetables, salt and time. Lacto-fermentation is safe and forgiving when you follow two rules: correct salt, everything under the brine.
gear: A wide-mouth jar with a loose lid or airlock
A weight to keep vegetables submerged
steps: Weigh the vegetables and use 2% of that weight in salt — this ratio is what makes it safe and is worth being precise about.
For sauerkraut, shred cabbage, mix with salt and massage until it releases enough brine to cover itself.
Pack tightly into the jar, pressing out air pockets, and weigh everything below the brine line.
Leave at room temperature, loosely covered or with an airlock so CO2 can escape, and burp daily if sealed.
Taste from day five onwards. When you like it, refrigerate to slow the fermentation down.
Learn the signs: cloudy brine and bubbling are good; fuzzy coloured mould on the surface means discard.
tips: Anything above the brine will spoil. Keep it all submerged, every day.
White film on the surface is usually harmless kahm yeast; fuzzy green, black or pink growth means throw it out.
Warmer ferments faster and tastes less complex. Cool and slow is better.
proof: A jar of sauerkraut you fermented, tasting sour and clean, that you are happy to serve to other people.
